gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera sets its rounded letters far apart, each one open-faced and traced with a plotter-pen line. Lexend Tera is at its best in that spacing, which the Arkhip heading, floating and unmodulated, echoes.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-lexend-zetta: Arkhip draws floating, unmodulated letters with a bent-paperclip c. Lexend Zetta is a tall-bodied sans with widely tracked, constant-width strokes, and that shared looseness with the heading is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-montserrat-alternat: Montserrat Alternates reads tight and chalky, its lowercase crowding toward the capital line. Montserrat Alternates handles dense, tall texture best, while Arkhip is best at spacious letters floating free of any modulation.
gen-dafont-burnstown-dam-poppins: Refined, with a hairline-crack gap and a tall lowercase, Burnstown Dam has closed letters. Poppins brings open, rope-loose curves and a sturdy lowercase, leaving Burnstown Dam to earn its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-cargo-poppins: Cargo comes in raw and striking, with open sidebearings and a barely open c, and little height difference between its cases. Closed against open is the draw, with Poppins the open half.
gen-dafont-chinese-rocks-poppins: Chinese Rocks has wire-cut strokes and almost no white space between glyphs, so it hits hard. And Poppins, plain sans with rope-loose curves and a sturdy lowercase, lets a paragraph run on without thick-thin flicker.
gen-dafont-chrome-poppins: Chrome collapses from heavy bowls to thread-thin curves in an instant. Poppins, plain sans with a marker-like line and rope-loose curves, lets paragraphs of text glide along without the jolt Chrome gives.
gen-dafont-cookies-poppins: Sweet and inviting, Cookies has a very large lowercase eye and apertures slim as a razor cut. But Poppins opens everything up, plain sans with a single-width, rolling-ball-pen line, and that closed-versus-open tension is the draw.
gen-dafont-cowboys-gf-cascadia-mono: Rustic and authoritative, Cowboys leaves big gaps between stems and traces each letter like a laser-etched line. Cascadia Mono, compact and pin-spaced, makes paragraphs read like a tidy row.
gen-dafont-cowboys-gf-julius-sans-one: Cowboys spaces its stems far apart and traces them in a laser-etched line. Julius Sans One, sans-serif with barely any difference between capital and lowercase height, lets text drift along in wide, open-ended curves.
